inputs: the ACTUAL tool names a real Codex CLI 0.154.0 session reports for itself: collaboration.spawn_agent, collaboration.followup_task (send + trigger), collaboration.send_message (send WITHOUT triggering), collaboration.interrupt_agent, collaboration.list_agents, collaboration.wait_agent
representations: the REALIZATIONS table read by realizationsCommand() and by pair-cli's own fallback message
SKILL.md's Step 0 table (row `codex`) and Step 3's `reuse` bullet, prose mirrors of the same two literals
cycle-coordinator.test.mjs AC6-w1/AC6-w2/AC7-w4, which pinned the WRONG literals as the expected behavior
consumers: every Codex-bound dispatch of pair-workflow-cycle, at Step 0's mandatory probe
the AC-6 fallback message shown to a maintainer when no realization binds
classes: C1 (the defect, live at inputHead before this fix) — dispatch: 'spawn_agent' never equals any real Codex tool name, so `tools.has('spawn_agent')` is always false against a real Codex toolset: `bound` is always undefined for Codex, and Step 0 HALTs `realization-unavailable` even though the session genuinely has an equivalent capability
C2 (target state) — dispatch: 'collaboration.spawn_agent' matches the real reported name, so the row binds correctly
interactions: I1 — the fix's resume value interacts with RESUME_ALIASES: collaboration.send_message is a real, present Codex tool that superficially resembles a resume primitive but does not trigger the sub-agent to act on the delivered message; including it in RESUME_ALIASES would let a resume silently succeed at the probe layer while never actually resuming any work downstream. Verified by reading the introspection transcript's own description of the tool ('without triggering it') rather than assumed from its name.

supportingEvidence.description: Live introspection of a real Codex CLI 0.154.0 session, run from this worktree, BEFORE any fix or dispatch was attempted against it — the actual authority this whole contract is derived from.
supportingEvidence.command: codex exec -c model="gpt-5.6-terra" -s read-only --skip-git-repo-check "List every distinct tool/function you have available to call right now, exactly as declared to you in this session... do you have ANY tool/capability to start, delegate to, or communicate with another separate agent session..."
supportingEvidence.observed: collaboration.spawn_agent — start a separate sub-agent session. collaboration.followup_task — send work to an existing sub-agent and trigger it. collaboration.send_message — message an existing agent without triggering it. collaboration.interrupt_agent — interrupt a running sub-agent. collaboration.list_agents — list live agents. collaboration.wait_agent — wait for agent updates. 'Yes: I can spawn, delegate to, message, interrupt, and wait on separate sub-agent sessions via the collaboration.* tools above.'
